text: Gold rose about 1.9% to near $3,954 on Monday, bouncing back from Friday's drop to a one-year low.
Silver gained about 3% to $50.63, back above $50, and the gold/silver ratio narrowed to about 78 from 79.4.
Gold miners outpaced gold: GDX closed up 2.7% at $79.15 and GDXJ up 2.3%, while the 3x GDXU gained 7.3%.
Brent settled down 7.6% at $104.77, its biggest one-day drop since July, on hopes of US–Iran talks that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Tech fell again on AI-spending worries: the Nasdaq dropped 1.1% and the S&P 500 0.5% to its lowest close since July 31, while the Dow rose 0.4%. QQQ lost 1.4% and TQQQ 4.1%.
The VIX rose about 9% to 21.15, back above 20, after Friday's 13% jump.
Apple closed down 1.8% before reporting better-than-expected quarterly results after the bell; its shares were modestly higher after hours.
